mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the octet rule with the duet rule?

options.A: The octet rule applies to all elements, requiring eight electrons in the valence shell, while the duet rule applies only to hydrogen and helium, requiring two electrons.
options.B: The octet rule applies only to metals, whereas the duet rule applies to non‑metals.
options.C: Both the octet and duet rules require eight electrons in the valence shell.
options.D: The octet rule is a special case of the duet rule for elements with atomic number greater than 10.

mcqs.answer: The octet rule applies to all elements, requiring eight electrons in the valence shell, while the duet rule applies only to hydrogen and helium, requiring two electrons.
mcqs.explanation: The octet rule states that atoms tend to achieve eight valence electrons, similar to noble gases. This rule is relevant for most elements beyond the first period. The duet rule is a special case for hydrogen and helium, which need only two electrons to fill their 1s orbital. Options B, C, and D misrepresent the scope and meaning of the rules.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Lewis symbols correctly represents a chlorine (Cl) atom?

options.A: Cl with three lone pairs and one unpaired electron
options.B: Cl with two lone pairs and three unpaired electrons

mcqs.answer: Cl with three lone pairs and one unpaired electron
mcqs.explanation: Chlorine belongs to group 17 and has seven valence electrons. In a Lewis symbol these are shown as three lone pairs (6 electrons) plus one single dot representing the seventh electron. Option B distributes the seven electrons incorrectly, while C and D show too many electrons.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct Lewis structure for a water (H₂O) molecule?

options.A: O with two lone pairs and two single bonds to H atoms
options.B: O with one lone pair and two double bonds to H atoms
options.C: O with three lone pairs and one single bond to an H atom
options.D: O with no lone pairs and two single bonds to H atoms

mcqs.answer: O with two lone pairs and two single bonds to H atoms
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen has six valence electrons; it forms two single covalent bonds with hydrogen (using two electrons) and retains the remaining four electrons as two lone pairs. This satisfies the octet rule for oxygen. Options B, C, and D violate the octet or give an impossible bonding arrangement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a limitation of the octet rule?

options.A: It cannot explain the bonding in molecules of elements in period 3 and beyond that have expanded octets.
options.B: It predicts the exact bond angles in all molecules.
options.C: It applies equally well to transition metals.

mcqs.answer: It cannot explain the bonding in molecules of elements in period 3 and beyond that have expanded octets.
mcqs.explanation: Elements such as sulfur, phosphorus, and silicon can accommodate more than eight electrons (expanded octet) because they have d‑orbitals. The simple octet rule fails for these cases. Options B, C, and D describe capabilities the octet rule does not possess.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the octet rule?

options.A: Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons so that they have eight electrons in their valence shell, achieving a noble gas configuration.
options.B: Atoms always share exactly two electrons with each other.
options.C: Only hydrogen atoms follow the octet rule.
options.D: The octet rule states that atoms must have exactly eight protons.

mcqs.answer: Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons so that they have eight electrons in their valence shell, achieving a noble gas configuration.
mcqs.explanation: The octet rule is a guideline stating that atoms are most stable when they possess eight electrons in their outermost shell, similar to noble gases. Options B, C, and D misstate the rule's meaning.

mcqs.question: Using Lewis symbols, how many valence electrons are present in a sulfur (S) atom?
mcqs.explanation: Sulfur is in group 16 of the periodic table, which means it has six valence electrons. In a Lewis symbol, these would be shown as six dots around the S symbol. The other numbers correspond to different groups.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Lewis structures correctly represents the nitrate ion (NO₃⁻)?

options.A: N central atom with one double bond to an O atom, and two single bonds to two O atoms each bearing a negative charge, with appropriate lone pairs.
options.B: N central atom with three single bonds to three O atoms, each O bearing a negative charge.
options.C: N double bonded to all three O atoms, no formal charges.
options.D: N with a triple bond to one O and single bonds to two O atoms.

mcqs.answer: N central atom with one double bond to an O atom, and two single bonds to two O atoms each bearing a negative charge, with appropriate lone pairs.
mcqs.explanation: The nitrate ion has a total of 24 valence electrons. The best resonance structure shows nitrogen forming one N=O double bond and two N–O single bonds; the singly bonded oxygens each carry a formal negative charge, giving the overall -1 charge. Option B gives an incorrect total charge distribution, C violates the octet on nitrogen, and D is not a valid resonance form.

mcqs.question: Which molecule is an example where the central atom does NOT obey the octet rule?
mcqs.explanation: Boron in BF₃ has only six valence electrons (three single B–F bonds) and therefore does not achieve an octet; this is a classic exception to the octet rule. CH₄, NH₃, and H₂O all satisfy the octet rule for the central atom.
